raw_response:
Well, let me think about this year. I've been doing cotton on these 16.1 mu since I married in — it's been five seasons now. My husband mostly works outside, so I handle most of the land with help from my mother-in-law and the kids when they're out of school. Six mouths to feed, so I can't afford a bad year.

Cotton is what everyone in our village grows on this side. The land isn't great for wheat-maize — too sandy in spots, and the water from the well isn't always strong enough to keep up with double-cropping. So cotton it is, like my neighbors.

I'll start getting ready in April. Usually I plant around 谷雨 time — mid to late April, when the soil warms up. Last year I planted on the early side and got caught by a cold snap, some seedlings didn't come up and I had to replant patches. This year I'll wait for steady warm weather, probably around April 20–25. I watch what 老王 next door does — he's been growing cotton twenty years, if he's planting, I plant.

For seed, I'll buy the same kind I got last year from the agro-shop in town — it's a 转基因 Bt hybrid, costs around 50 yuan per mu but the bollworm doesn't wreck it. I don't save seed, it's hybrid so it wouldn't work.

For fertilizer — I put down compound fertilizer before planting, one of the 15-15-15 bags, about one bag (50 kg) per mu as base. Then when the cotton starts flowering, in late June or early July, I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. That's what most people here do. If I had more money I'd put more, but a bag of compound is already 140 yuan, so with 16 mu that's a lot of cash up front.

I lay plastic mulch with the planter — everyone does this, keeps the soil warm and the weeds down. The village has someone with a mulch-laying machine, I pay him to come do it, about 30 yuan per mu.

Irrigation — I have the well share with three other families, so I get my turn. For cotton I usually water once before planting to moisten the bed, then once in July when it's flowering and hot, then maybe once more in August if it doesn't rain. Three times total, sometimes two if the summer rains are good. Pumping costs add up — diesel for the pump is maybe 30 yuan per mu each time.

Pesticide — cotton needs a lot. Aphids in spring, bollworm even with Bt, red spider mite in hot dry weeks. I spray maybe 5 or 6 times across the season. I buy from the shop, whatever they recommend. Probably 100 yuan a mu total on chemicals.

Tillage — I hire the neighbor with the tractor to plow and rotovate before planting. About 80 yuan per mu all in.

Labor — this is the hard part. Picking cotton is the killer. Three picks, maybe four, from September into October. My mother-in-law and I do most of it, and my older kid helps after school. For the last pick I sometimes hire a couple of women from the village to help, maybe 10 days of hired labor at 100 yuan a day. Family labor is probably 150 days across the year, between me and my mother-in-law mainly.

Yield — last year I got about 250 kg of lint per mu, which was okay. The year before was better, maybe 280. I'm hoping for 250 again this year, not going to plan for more than that — better to be surprised than disappointed. Price last year was decent, around 7 yuan per catty for seed cotton, so I'll hope that holds.
